findings.title: Database backup artifacts contain password hashes and inherit default file permissions
findings.rootCause: The SQL/JSON-Lines backup export (CLI db backup) and pg_dump output store complete rows, including users.password_hash, and are written with the process umask. No explicit 0600 permission or encryption is applied.
findings.confidenceRationale: Direct source reading of exportBackup and scripts/backup.sh; no runtime inspection of resulting file modes.
findings.attackerControl: Local user or process with read access to the backups directory
findings.impact: Offline password-hash disclosure enables offline guessing; order/user data disclosure.
findings.scenario: A backup file created during class or operations is readable by another local account and copied off the machine.
findings.recommendation: Create backups with mode 0600 (or a dedicated directory 0700), document encryption-at-rest for production, and avoid shipping backups with the repo.

challenge.controls: backups/ is gitignored and documented as operator-only
challenge.counterevidence: local classroom demo has no multi-user host threat model
challenge.conclusion: survives as a low-severity operational hygiene issue

findings.title: Rate limiting state is process-local; restart or a second instance resets counters
findings.rootCause: createRateLimiter keeps failures in an in-memory Map keyed by account+IP and IP. The application is documented as single-instance; a restart clears lockouts and a second replica would not share counters.
findings.confidenceRationale: Direct source reading; R3 explicitly designs a single-instance demo and documents the boundary.
findings.attackerControl: Ability to wait for a restart or to target a deployment with multiple replicas
findings.impact: Online password guessing budget resets; brute-force protection is weaker than a shared store.
findings.scenario: Attacker waits for a service restart or deployment scale-out and retries the password list.
findings.recommendation: Keep for R3 and document the single-instance boundary; for production, move counters to a shared store (or edge/WAF rate limiting).

challenge.callers: checked login service and compose deployment
challenge.counterevidence: R3 declares no horizontal scaling and a single replica in compose
challenge.conclusion: survives as a scoped limitation, not a functional bug

findings.title: Local compose does not terminate TLS; cookie Secure flag depends on deployer configuration
findings.rootCause: The default docker-compose.yml exposes HTTP on 4175 and defaults COOKIE_SECURE=0 for classroom. Production requires APP_ENV=production plus COOKIE_SECURE=1, but TLS/HTTPS itself is delegated to an external reverse proxy and is not part of the delivered compose file.
findings.confidenceRationale: Direct reading of compose env defaults and config.mjs production checks; no external TLS terminator is shipped.
findings.attackerControl: Network attacker on the path between browser and host
findings.impact: Session cookie could travel over plaintext if the deployer exposes 4175 directly.
findings.scenario: Operator publishes the compose port to a LAN/WAN without a TLS proxy; login credentials and session cookie are sent in clear text.
findings.recommendation: Document that the delivered stack is localhost/demo only; for deployment terminate TLS at an external proxy and keep COOKIE_SECURE=1 enforced in production (already checked).

challenge.callers: checked compose ports and production config validation
challenge.counterevidence: PRD explicitly excludes HTTPS certificates for local compose
challenge.conclusion: survives as a documented deployment boundary

findings.title: CLI db restore trusts operator-supplied JSON Lines without schema-version compatibility check
findings.rootCause: importBackup validates the meta.type/app marker but not that meta.schemaVersion matches the running binary; a backup from a different schema version could be partially applied before failing, though it runs in one transaction.
findings.confidenceRationale: Direct source reading; transactional rollback limits impact to restore failure rather than corruption.
findings.attackerControl: Operator/supply-chain control over the backup file
findings.impact: Restore fails or produces schema/data mismatch that is detected only by later checks.
findings.scenario: An old backup file is restored after a future schema change; insert order/columns no longer match.
findings.recommendation: Compare meta.schemaVersion with the current migration version and refuse mismatches with a clear error; add a backup format version test.

challenge.counterevidence: R3 ships a single schema version, so mismatch is not reachable in classroom
challenge.conclusion: survives as a low-severity forward-compatibility gap
